subject: Ariba/Coupa portal field exception & MSA redline coordination
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@novamed.com>, Tom Gallagher <tom.gallagher@supplyhub.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T08:15:00-04:00
Subject: Ariba/Coupa onboarding: field mapping issues and MSA redline

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for starting the onboarding process. We hit a couple of blockers while trying to register Redwood in our Ariba and Coupa supplier portals and legal has flagged a redline in the MSA that blocks procurement from moving forward. Quick summary:

- Ariba rejects the registration because Redwood's "Tax ID" field doesn't match our expected VAT format (Novamed requires VAT with country prefix for suppliers registered in EU).
- Coupa mapping is failing on PO import: our backend expects BuyerOrderNumber in the XML, but Redwood's PO sends BuyerReference; our EDI team says this breaks automated invoicing.
- Legal attached an MSA with a modified liability clause (Novamed proposed increasing the liability to 2x fees) — our GC says this needs negotiation before signature.

I've attached the redlined MSA and the draft order form. Can your team advise:
1) Can you provide a mapping spec for Ariba/Coupa fields (VAT vs TaxID, remit-to vs remit_to_bank)?
2) Is there a temporary PO-field mapping we can apply on our side to accept BuyerReference?
3) Who from Redwood legal/sales can own the MSA negotiation?

We want to avoid manual cutovers if possible — our preferred go-live window is 2026-09-20 to align with our billing cycle.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement - Novamed Health
elena.rossi@novamed.com
+44 20 8123 4567

Elena — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Karthik (onboarding/ops) to help. Quick answers up front:

- We can produce a field-mapping spec for both Ariba and Coupa. I'll attach a working spreadsheet and call out the VAT vs TaxID behavior for EU suppliers.
- For the PO element mismatch: we can push a minor variant so our generated POs include BuyerOrderNumber in an alternate field, but that will be a short-term workaround — we should agree a canonical mapping.
- Marissa will lead legal on the MSA negotiation.

Action items I propose:
1) Karthik to share the technical mapping doc and propose a temporary mapping rule by EOD tomorrow.
2) Marissa to review the Novamed redlines and confirm which clauses are non-starters vs negotiable.
3) Elena/Procurement: confirm whether Novamed can accept a temporary manual PO reconciliation for 1-2 billing cycles if we can't finish the XML change by 2026-09-20.

We want to keep the go-live window if possible — if the mapping has a small catch-up we can coordinate a phased onboarding.

Cheers,
Jonas
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Ariba/Coupa onboarding: field mapping issues and MSA redline

Hi all — I dug into our PO and vendor export pipelines this morning. Notes and proposed workarounds below.

1) VAT / Tax ID (Ariba) - Ariba's registration UI has a free-text Tax ID field; for EU buyers Novamed validates pattern "^([A-Z]{2}\\d{8,12})$" (country prefix + digits). Redwood currently stores Tax ID without country prefix for some entities.
  - Short-term: we can accept a vendor registration with Tax ID in the existing format if Novamed sets a portal exception flag; ops can approve manually.
  - Medium-term: we'll update our vendor profile export to include the country prefix on VAT for all EU-registered suppliers (ETA 2 business days).

2) PO XML element mismatch (Coupa / EDI) - Your EDI team expects <BuyerOrderNumber> while our generated XML currently populates <BuyerReference>. This is an easy schema change on our side:
  - Option A (fast): add duplicate element <BuyerOrderNumber> with same value as <BuyerReference>. ETA: 48-72 hours if we can schedule a small release.
  - Option B (Novamed-side): map <BuyerReference> to BuyerOrderNumber in your parser — we can share the ariba-field-mapping-specs.xlsx for your EDI team to test.

3) Remit-to banking format- Some portals require structured: bank_country, bank_code, iban, swift. We can export a CSV sample (attached remit-to-bank-sample.csv) for your portal team to validate.

Attachments: ariba-field-mapping-specs.xlsx; remit-to-bank-sample.csv

If Novamed can set a one-time portal exception for Tax ID validation and accept Option A for PO XML duplication, we can meet the 2026-09-20 go-live. Otherwise we propose a phased go-live for vendor registration first and PO automation in the following week.

Happy to set a 30-min technical sync tomorrow with your EDI folks.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Onboarding Engineer — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Ariba/Coupa onboarding: field mapping issues and MSA redline

Hi Elena — I reviewed the Novamed redlines and here are the legal positions from Redwood: 

1) Liability cap — Novamed proposes 2x fees. Redwood position: we are comfortable with a liability cap tied to fees but capped at a fixed amount. Proposed compromise: liability limited to the greater of (1) aggregate fees paid in 12 months or (2) $1,000,000. If Novamed insists on 2x fees without a hard cap, that's a non-starter for us.

2) Indemnity — we can accept customer indemnity for third-party claims arising from customer's data or instructions, but Redwood seeks mutuality for IP infringement claims.

3) Data Processing / Security — Redwood will sign the DPA addendum; we need confirmation of required retention periods and whether Novamed requires specific SOC-2 artifacts. We can provide SOC 2 Type II report via an approved portal link; we prefer not to send raw artifacts via email.

4) Payment terms — order form shows Net45. Finance prefers Net30. If Novamed insists on Net45, we can consider it with a 2% early-pay discount or a 30-day payment milestone tied to initial invoice.

Next steps I recommend:
- Elena / Procurement to confirm whether Novamed can accept our proposed liability compromise.
- If accepted, we'll prepare a tracked-change MSA (clean + tracked redlines) and send via DocuSign for signature.
- Legal and procurement should align on whether a manual PO reconciliation window is acceptable for 1-2 cycles while ops implements the XML duplicate field change.

Please let me know a good time for a short negotiation call this week if you prefer to discuss live.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
